campaigns.description: The automations to import, at most 50. People are never read from these objects.

actions.description: The top-level `actions` array from the same response, every step of the automation.

campaign.description: The `campaign` object from Customer.io's `GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/campaigns/{campaign_id}` (Journeys UI API, what the Customer.io CLI and MCP read). Must include `id`, `type`, `edges` and the trigger fields.

templates.description: The message templates the actions point at, from `GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/templates/{template_id}`: a list of template objects, or an object keyed by template id. Leave them out when the project stored a Customer.io App API key: PostHog then reads the content from Customer.io itself. Without either, messages import with empty content.

dry_run.description: When true, translate and check the automations but save nothing, to preview the import.

layouts.description: Customer.io layout id to the layout's `body`, from `GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/layouts/{layout_id}`. An email whose template names a `layout_id` is wrapped in that layout at `{{ content }}`.

segment_cohorts.description: Customer.io segment id to the PostHog cohort that replaces it. Segment triggers and segment conditions with no cohort here are left for the team to set.

segments.description: Customer.io segments, without members: ids, names and types, so the notes can name each segment and flag static ones, and the rules of each segment the automations check, so the import can turn it into a realtime cohort.

conditions.description: The segment's rules: the `conditions` object from `GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/segments/{segment_id}`. Never its members. With rules, a real import turns a dynamic segment the automations check into a realtime cohort when every rule has an exact cohort condition, and uses that cohort.

type.description: The segment's type: `dynamic`, or `static` for a hand-made list.

sender_identities.description: Customer.io sender identities, from `GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}/identities?type=email`. Each email gets the PostHog sender with the same address.

email.description: The address the sender sends from.

id.description: The sender identity's id, which templates name in `from_identity_id`.

snippets.description: Customer.io snippet name to its content, inlined where a message uses `{{ snippets.name }}`. When PostHog reads the message content with a stored Customer.io App API key, it reads the snippets too.

source.description:
The tool the automations come from.

* `customerio` - Customer.io
